notes:
This is in compound forms in the past and future tenses.
a.present tense.
Pattern: SP + shi + VS in present continuous, unless verb takes Ashiteekhanga.

past tense.
Yakhaba/abeele/yabeele/yali nashiteekhanga. - She is still cooking.
Yakhaba/abeele/yabeele/yali nashisinjile. - He was still standing.

c.future tenses.
Pattern: SP + "to be" in future tense + ni + SP + shi + VS in present continuous (unless verb takes past tense)
Alaba/nabe/yakhabe/aliba nashiteekhanga. - She will still be cooking.
Alaba/nabe/yakhabe/aliba nashisinjile. - He will still be standing.

4.Olwa ebiamo biabo biâli nibienjile, ebiefu biâli nibishianganga

6.Inywe nimukofuile, abana-beenyu bakhae nibashili abadukka

Exercise 26

Kalukhasia muLuluvia:
1.After the water in the 'spring ' was.gone. (disappeared), that in the river was still'(in) there.
2.When our milk was finished, theirs was still here.(i.e., they still had some).
3.After these grasshoppers were hunted, the children were still hunting others.
4.When their fruit had ripened, ours was still ripening.
5.After her sieve was worn out, mine was still good.
6.When you (pl.) have grown old, your children will still be young people.
7.When these strainers have become old, those will still be new.
8.After these eggs have spoiled, those others yonder will still be good.
9.When my flock has finished grazing in this pasture today, the other one will still be grazing in it.
10.After this fire has gone out, the children will still be studying their lessons.
